Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Confirming the numbers you captured are in the right ballpark. A few clarifications and context from our side: 

Token bands: we expect ~10M tokens/month in our internal alpha (Q3), moving to 25–35M by Q4 as we open to more customers, and ~50M+ for certain enterprise customers. The biggest swing will be prompt length variability in summarization flows (avg tokens per call could be 150–400).

Budget: for the pilot we have a budget envelope of $40k–$90k/month depending on performance and latency guarantees. If the numbers look aligned we can push to expand the pilot. Procurement: copied procurement for SOC2 + contract timeline questions.

Unit economics asks:
- Can you show sample $/1M token price points (hosted vs reserved) and the associated $/feature for average token sizes (150 / 250 / 400)?

- Example CAC payback sensitivity — we typically target sub-9 month payback for new self-serve features. Helpful if you can model 6/9/12 month payback scenarios given per-feature inference cost.

Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — pricing scenarios & $/feature examples

Alex — thanks for the clarity. I put together the starter package and attached a simple pricing model (Redwood_pricing_model_1M_tokens.xlsx) with three scenarios. Highlights below — will walk through these in the meeting: 

Assumptions (simple):
- $/1M tokens (hosted spot rates to reserved discounts): low tier $1,200 / 1M, mid $900 / 1M, committed reserved $600 / 1M. (These are illustrative; final will depend on model variant/latency SLO and contract term.)
- Per-token math: at $600/1M -> $0.0006 / token; at $900/1M -> $0.0009 / token; at $1,200/1M -> $0.0012 / token.

$/feature sensitivity (typical tokens per call):
- 150 tokens -> $0.09 (at $600/1M), $0.135 (at $900), $0.18 (at $1,200)
- 250 tokens -> $0.15, $0.225, $0.30
- 400 tokens -> $0.24, $0.36, $0.48

Margin impact examples (assume feature price $0.99):
- For 250-token feature at $600/1M tokens, inference cost $0.15 => gross margin ~84% before infra/ops/support/commissions. If you price feature lower or include bundle discounts, margin tightens — this is where reserved pricing matters.

CAC payback worked example (back-of-envelope):
- If CAC = $45 and incremental ARPU from the paid feature = $6/mo, payback = 7.5 months.
- If the feature uses 250 tokens and inference cost per feature $0.15, monthly per-user variable cost = $0.15 * average uses per month (assume 4) = $0.60/mo. Net contribution = $6 - $0.60 = $5.40/mo -> payback ~8.3 months.

Key levers to hit 30–40% gross margin target:
1) Move to reserved/committed pricing bands to reduce $/1M from spot to committed rates.
2) Optimize prompts & caching (prefix caching for repeated context) to reduce average tokens per call.
3) Apply feature-level pricing or throttling for heavy users to control variable cost.

Attachments included: Redwood_pricing_model_1M_tokens.xlsx (spreadsheet with scenario tabs), FintechX_MAPlist.xlsx (updated), SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf

Proposed agenda for Tue 7/14 10:00am PT (30–45m):

- Walk through pricing scenarios and $/feature sensitivity (Marissa/Rishi) — 15m
- Action items: procurement checklist & next steps for reserved commitment term (Marissa/Rishi) — 10m

If this looks good I’ll send a calendar invite.
